messages:
jess: FYI canary for v3.4.0 is spiking — p95 latency up ~5x and 500s climbing. Deploy-bot flagged it at 1976543198. Thinking we should hold the rollout and consider rollback to v3.3.9.

omar: ACK. Can you paste the deploy-bot alert?

deploy-bot: ALERT: canary/v3.4.0 - p95 520ms -> 2700ms, 5xx rate 0.3% -> 4.1% in last 3m. auto-rollback-threshold=3.0% (enabled=false for canaries).

marta: Do we know if this is a model change or infra kernel path? Any recent kernel flags/quantization toggles?

jess: This build had the kernel selection tweak and a new kv-cache prewarm on the runtime. No model changes.

tina: If kv-cache prewarm is the trigger, rollback to v3.3.9 (no prewarm) seems safest. But note there's a DB migration scheduled in 20m — we should avoid rolling during the window.

alex: Support here — we have a handful of customers on dedicated pools; none alerted yet. If we rollback, do we expect connection churn? Need to update release notes / status page.

sre-oncall: Agreed with Tina. Suggest partial rollback: pin canary traffic back to v3.3.9 and pause new canary releases until we verify. Manual rollback since auto-rollback is disabled for canaries.

omar: Steps I propose: 1) Hold all further canary pushes (release manager lock). 2) Run partial rollback on canary slice only: `redwoodctl rollout set --model-service canary --version v3.3.9 --slice 10%` 3) Monitor 5m. 4) If stable, promote pin and schedule a full rollback outside the DB migration window.

jess: +1 to that. Add comms: Post incident note + short blurb to #status and ping CS. Marta, can you draft the customer-facing note?

marta: Drafting now. Short note: "We've paused the v3.4.0 canary after observing elevated latency. We're rolling canary traffic back to v3.3.9 while we investigate. No data loss expected. We'll provide updates."

tina: Operational checklist for the rollback (for the thread):
• run `redwoodctl rollout set --model-service canary --version v3.3.9 --slice 10% --reason "canary latency spike"`
• verify canary p95 < 600ms and 5xx < 0.5% within 5m
• if good, expand slice 10% -> 50% over 10m then to 100% after DB migration window ends
• capture telemetry and assign to eng-runtime for root cause (kernel selection toggle + kv prewarm)
• open PR to revert kernel flag in staging for retest

alex: I'll prepare the status page entry and ping the affected customers with the draft.

sre-oncall: I'll coordinate the rollback window and own the deployment commands in case we need to force revert. If anything goes wrong, escalate to ops-lead and we can initiate a full cluster pin.

omar: Executing partial rollback now (handing off to deploy agent).

deploy-bot: COMMAND: `redwoodctl rollout set --model-service canary --version v3.3.9 --slice 10% --meta "rollback: canary latency spike"` — started

deploy-bot: STATUS: slice update succeeded, 10% -> v3.3.9 in 12s.

jess: Monitoring metrics — p95 dropped to ~580ms, 5xx down to 0.45% on the slice. Good sign.

marta: Posted update to #status and sent customer pings.

tina: Proceed with expansion plan after 10m stable check. We will not touch full rollout until after DB migration window closes.

sre-oncall: Noted — standing by for expansion or rollback back to v3.4.0 if needed. Assigning a postmortem to eng-runtime.

omar: Filing short internal note / rollback tag in release notes: `v3.4.0: canary rollback to v3.3.9 due to runtime latency regression; investigation ongoing.`

jess: Thanks everyone. If the root cause points to the kernel flag, we'll prepare a hotfix build and a controlled relaunch. For now the canary is pinned and customers are informed. :white_check_mark:
